messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Below is an up‑to‑date snapshot (as of May 2026) of key Texas traffic laws you’ll encounter whether you’re a resident, visitor, commercial driver, or simply curious. I’ve grouped them into major categories—speed & road rules, vehicle equipment, conduct, penalties, and special provisions—to make it easy to find what matters most to you. --- ### 1️⃣ General Road Rules | Rule | What It Means | |------|---------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary from 35–75 mph depending on area.
• Rural interstate highways: 70–80 mph (often 65 mph if “no sign”).
• Urban freeways: typically 55–60 mph unless posted otherwise.
• School zones: 25 mph during school hours (or when signs indicate). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield at uncontrolled intersections, crosswalks, railroad crossings, and roundabouts.
• At stop signs, all vehicles must come to a complete halt before proceeding. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep left lane except when passing or turning right.
• Use turn lanes only for intended turns. | | **Headlights** | • Must be used between sunset and sunrise, after dark, or whenever visibility < 200 ft. | --- ### 2️⃣ Vehicle Equipment Requirements | Requirement | Details | |-------------|---------| | **Seat Belts** | All occupants must wear belts. Failure → $50 fine + possible points. | | **Child Safety Seats** | Children under 8 years *and* weighing ≤ 40 lb must be secured in approved child seats. | | **Lights/Signals** | Working headlights, brake lights, reverse lights, turn signals, hazard lights. | | **Windshield Wipers** | Functional wiper blades required in rainy conditions. | | **Tires** | Proper tread depth (≥ 2 mm), correct pressure, no visible damage. | | **License Plate** | Front plate mandatory since 2015; rear plate optional but recommended. | | **Vehicle Registration** | Display current registration sticker on front windshield. | | **Insurance** | Minimum liability coverage: \$30k bodily injury per person / \$60k total per accident; property damage \$15k. | --- ### 3️⃣ Driver Conduct Laws | Behavior | Penalty | |----------|--------| | **Texting While Driving** | First offense – $100 fine + 1 point. Repeat offenses increase fines ($250 first repeat, $500 second repeat). | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | Blood alcohol concentration ≥ 0.08% triggers DUI charges. Penalties include license suspension, jail time, and hefty fees. | | **Reckless Driving** | Defined as operating a vehicle with willful disregard for safety. Can lead to felony charges. | | **Failure to Stop at Red Light/Straight‑ahead Intersections** | Fine $150 plus potential points. | | **Using Mobile Phone Without Hands‑Free Mode** | Same penalty as texting. | | **Improper Lane Change** | If performed without signaling or causing obstruction, may result in a ticket. | | **Parking Violations** | Parking in handicap spaces without proper permit results in a $300 fine. | --- ### 4️⃣ Commercial Drivers (CDLs) | Issue | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Hours of Service (HOS)** | Max 11 hrs driving within a 14‑hr period; 10‑hour rest break required. | | **Electronic Logging Device (ELD)** | Mandatory for trucks over 26,000 lbs gross weight. | | **Drug Testing** | Pre-employment, random, post-accident testing mandated. | | **Safety Rating System** | Companies accrue points based on violations; high scores trigger audits. | --- ### 5️⃣ Special Provisions | Provision | Explanation | |-----------|--------------| | **Texas DOT’s “No Sign Speed Limit” Law** | In rural areas where no limit sign exists, default speed is 70 mph (unless state highway authority sets lower). | | **School Bus Stops** | Vehicles must stop fully behind red flashing lights until children board/alight. | | **Bicycle Lanes** | Cyclists have same rights as motorists; drivers must yield appropriately. | | **Motorcycle Helmet Law** | Helmets required for riders under 18; adults encouraged but not legally enforced. | | **Pedestrian Right-of-Way** | Pedestrians always have priority at marked crosswalks regardless of signal status. | --- ### 📌 Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Situation | Action Needed | |-----------|----------------| | **Entering a new county** | Check local signage for updated speed limits. | | **Nighttime driving** | Turn on low beams; switch to high beams beyond 1 mile away from other cars. | | **Encountering a stopped emergency vehicle** | Pull over to the far side of the roadway and wait until cleared. | | **Seeing a school bus stopping** | Do NOT pass the bus until its doors close and lights cease flashing. | | **Receiving a ticket** | Pay online within 7 days to avoid additional late fees. | --- ### 🔍 Where to Find Official Texts | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | Texas Transportation Code (Title 54) | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/?link=TXSTC&chapter=54 | | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) – Traffic Regulations | https://www.txdmv.gov/motorist-resources/road-safety-and-regulations | | Texas Highway Patrol – Enforcement Guidelines | https://tpd.state.tx.us/enforcement-guidelines | Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper dives into any subsection—for example, detailed DUI statutes, how points affect insurance premiums, or recent changes to electronic logging device regulations!
